title: service-mix token-tilt experiments (wip)
content:
Background:
This is a working workbook / narrative for an experiments-driven approach to shifting request service-mix across model families and regions to find near-term token-cost reductions while respecting latency SLOs and quality constraints for Hosted API customers. The aim is not a single canonical pricing change, but a set of operational knobs + telemetry changes we can iterate on and validate in Q2.

High-level hypothesis:
- By nudging a small percent of traffic from high-ppk low-latency model variants to slightly slower but much cheaper variants in specific regions we can reduce marginal COGS by ~6–12% without materially increasing 95th latency for paying customers.
- Gains are concentrated in long-tail sequence-length workloads and prompt-heavy customers where prefix caching and batching can be preserved.

Key spreadsheet tabs (to build / validate):
1) assumptions - single-page list of the numbers below (amortization windows, GPU license, power, network egress, average seq length per route)
2) region-model-costs - per-region per-model PPK baseline and components (gpu-amort, power, egress, infra share, orchestration overhead)
3) request-mix - customer cohort or route-level distribution (seq len histogram, tokens/request, concurrency pattern)
4) tilt-scenarios - knobs for shifting X% traffic from model A -> model B by region, with capacity and failover checks
5) sensitivity - monte-carlo-ish sweeps across seq length, batch size, and cache hit rates
6) rollout-plan - canary thresholds, monitoring hooks, rollback criteria, experiment ids

Minimal column schema for region-model-costs tab (spreadsheet column headings):
- model_family | model_variant | region | gpu_type | gpu_amort_ppk | power_ppk | egress_ppk | infra_overhead_ppk | kv_cache_savings_ppk | observed_p95_latency_ms | compatible_batch_window_ms | quantized_flag | notes

Example snapshot (typed-in example rows):
model_family | variant | region | gpu_type | gpu_amort_ppk | power_ppk | egress_ppk | infra_overhead_ppk | kv_cache_savings_ppk | p95_latency_ms
Redwood-7B     | v1-q4_0   | us-west1 | A100-80G   | 0.0078        | 0.0016   | 0.0009  | 0.0007            | -0.0025              | 48
Open-13B       | v1-fp16   | eu-west1 | H100-80G   | 0.0195        | 0.0038   | 0.0012  | 0.0014            | -0.0000              | 62
Llama-2-70B    | v2-q8_0   | us-east1 | H100-80G   | 0.0410        | 0.0086   | 0.0015  | 0.0025            | -0.0060              | 74

Formulas (spreadsheet pseudocode):
- raw_ppk = gpu_amort_ppk + power_ppk + egress_ppk + infra_overhead_ppk - kv_cache_savings_ppk
- adjusted_ppk_with_batching = raw_ppk / (1 + effective_batch_multiplier) ; where effective_batch_multiplier = avg_batch_size / baseline_batch
- route_margin = price_per_token - adjusted_ppk_with_batching ; price_per_token is from pricing SKU mapping

Tilt scenario example (narrative):
- scenario A: shift 8% of long-tail requests in eu-west1 from Open-13B-fp16 -> Redwood-7B-q4_0 during off-peak window (00:00–08:00 UTC). Assumptions: cache hit preserved at 92%; effective batch size increases by 1.25x.
- expected delta: eu-west1 region-weighted ppk reduction = 0.0034 -> ~8.3% unit cost drop for that workload slice; projected net margin uplift depending on price tier: small enterprise SKU sees +0.7ppt gross margin.

Capacity & safety checks (to implement in sheet):
- available_slots_by_region_model (derived from infra telemetry; placeholder column now)
- fallthrough_policy: if target model capacity < needed then route will use fallback variant with higher ppk and trace flag
- latency-bucket constraint: ensure 95th latency delta per route <= 10% absolute or <= 50ms, whichever is smaller

Measurements to wire up (linked_artifacts placeholders):
- perf traces: agent:perf/trace-ids (JIRA-OPT-219)
- billing alignment: finance mapping doc (CONFLUENCE-4567)
- experiment telemetry: slack channel #optimize-token-econ

Sensitivity ideas to add to sheet (WIP):
- quantization delta sensitivity: vary q8 vs q4 delta to see where cost wins vanish when quality loss requires fallback
- cold-cache effect: simulate initial requests after cache purge vs steady-state cache hit
- seq length tides: some customers shift median seq length between hours—look for low-cost routing during short token windows

Open questions / TODOs (owner tags inline):
- [Avery] reconcile A100 vs H100 amort numbers with infra team (expected 2025-03-07)
- [Marcus] add per-region egress discounts from cloud contracts (Q1 pricing)
- [Sofia] sample 3 customers for a pilot (one PLG, one enterprise chat, one embeddings-heavy) and export route histograms (deadline 2025-03-11)
- [Liam] implement script to produce available_slots_by_region_model from capacity API (prototype by 2025-03-10)
- add small column for expected quality-recall drop metric (we need a simple scalar to compare)

Rollout playbook draft (short):
1) Small canary (1–3% traffic) for non-critical routes, 24h minimum, monitor p95, error-rate, token-costs, and quality-check prompts.
2) If p95 increases > 20ms or quality metric decreases by > 1.5% revert immediately.
3) Gradual ramp to 25% over 48h if all green, continue to 90% (or maintain split) with automated rollback.

Notes on presentation and next steps:
- This doc is intentionally spreadsheet-first; the next deliverable is a compact dashboard (Console) slice showing per-route ppk delta and rolling 95th latency for each tilt experiment id.
- Goal for Q2: validate at least two tilt strategies that net positive ROI after monitoring/rollback costs.

Recent changes log:
- 2025-02-20: added quantization sensitivity row and draft formulas for adjusted_ppk_with_batching.
- 2025-02-28: tightened latency-bucket constraint language per SRE input.
- 2025-03-04: added example snapshot rows and collaborator TODOs.

If you hack on the sheet, please add a short note to this doc with a date and the change summary so the next reviewer can follow the thread.
